title_original: Fake Calendar Invites Target Thousands of Organizations in Microsoft Credential-Phishing Campaign
description: A calendar invite is one of the most routine messages in the modern workplace. It lands in the inbox, asks for a few seconds of attention, and is rarely questioned. Attackers know this, and they are now using fake meeting invitations to steal Microsoft account credentials. We have identified several large-scale phishing campaigns that abuse fake calendar invites to harvest credentials. Some arrive as an .ics attachment (example 1). The file is valid calendar data, so the attack abuses calendar features and user trust without exploiting a software vulnerability. title_original: Researchers Uncover Thousands of Phishing Domains Hiding Behind Inactive Pages
description: A domain returns a blank page. Maybe a generic “Not Found” message. There is no login form, suspicious branding, or obvious phishing content to investigate. Yet the phishing site may still be there. Check Point Exposure Management researchers uncovered a large scale, multi region phishing infrastructure designed to conceal active campaigns behind seemingly inactive domains. Starting with a handful of phishing URLs, the investigation identified a repeatable technical fingerprint that ultimately connected the activity to thousands of rotating domains targeting organizations and users across multiple regions. The infrastructure uses regional paths, localization, session controls, and token gated access to determine […]The postResearchers Uncover Thousands of Phishing Domains Hiding Behind Inactive Pagesappeared first onCheck Point Blog.
